closing.reason: All checks were run live in pgpm_prv-15 against both trees. (1) Entry points: only two archive paths reach a strategy, _archive_step (install.sql 5447) and scripts/archive_partition_whole.sql (161), and both go through the same changed hold. Neither pgpm_archive nor pgpm_hypertable calls _run_archive_strategy. Round 1's V-01 (a mark WITH its record, detach landed, archiving configured afterwards) is closed on the scheduled tick: the hold answers by pg_partition_ancestors alone, so no strategy is handed the detached table (not one reading through the parent, not _archive_noop, not a custom fn reading by oid), nothing is recorded, and retire() keeps the table. Older-install states: a mark with no record behaves as #1259's main case and is covered. A mark with a record whose job never ran leaves the partition attached, so it is read normally; if it is then detached by hand it is skipped with the remedy and nothing is recorded. An unanchored MARKED row is asked through its name (the coalesce). (2) A detach landing between the hold and the strategy: built as a two-session probe in which pgpm's dispatched DETACH ... CONCURRENTLY first transaction commits while the strategy waits (the pending flag was observed committed). On PG15 in this path the read through the parent still returned all 3 rows and the ledger recorded rows_archived 3, so nothing was lost on either tree. Not filed; the probe is kept in the verifier's scratch. (3) The surviving path, V-01: an UNANCHORED, UNMARKED row (child_oid null, the state an upgrade from before #421 leaves; set by hand as the fixture) whose write-blocked table was detached by hand. The head passes the hold a null oid (coalesce(r.child_oid, case when r.retiring_at is not null then v_now::oid end)) and the hold answers true. The table is handed to the strategy, [0,20) is recorded covered with rows_archived 0, and after the documented remedy (attach it back) retention drops it: rows 1, 2 and 15 are lost. Same result on the base and the head (pre_existing). The archive script has the same line (162). This contradicts the body's 'Neither archive path ... hands a strategy a table that is not a partition of its parent as of the hold's lock, whatever its mark', although the hold's comment carves unanchored rows out. Its mechanism is #705's open archive bullet (the archive step reaching an operator-detached table), so the coordinator may instead rule it known_open #705 and have the body's sentence narrowed. It is not #1259's mark mechanism. (4) Mutations: ACC-01 fails only on the combined retirement_mark_readers_whole; each single mutation alone passes it, which the body explains. The rebuilt ACC-02 fails on archive_hold_vouches_detached_retirement, so that mutation puts back round 1's defect. (5) ACC-02 is premise_removed: on the head it fails only at LIVENESS 5 (the drop no longer happens) and at check 7 (rows looked for only in the parent and the sink, while they survive in the kept detached table). Rebuilt as claims/ACC/ACC-02/repro.verified.sql, which pins no coverage for the detached monolith, rows 1, 2 and 15 present in the detached table (by oid) or the archive, skip_archive over [0,20) with the ATTACH remedy, and the remedy as typed archiving the rows before the drop; LIVENESS is kept. Results: BASE fails (5, 6, 7, 9 and LIVENESS 8; LIVENESS 1-4 ok); HEAD passes 9/9; MUTANT archive_hold_vouches_detached_retirement fails (5, 6, 7, 9; LIVENESS 1-4 ok).
